HOW TO PLAY

Turn-based artillery. Put shells on the other tank before it puts them on you. Everything below is optional depth — the first two cards are all you need to start.

Taking a shot

  • Drag anywhere on the battlefield to aim the barrel.
  • The angle is measured off your hull, not the horizon — where you park changes the shot.
  • Hold SPACE or the FIRE button to build power, release to shoot.
  • Q cancels a shot you have started charging.
  • W / S nudge the barrel finely.

Driving

  • A / D or the arrow buttons drive you.
  • Fuel is a budget of ground covered, refilled every turn.
  • Slopes cost more fuel and slow you down — but nothing is too steep to climb.
  • Moving to dodge, reach a crate, or escape fire is often worth more than a shot.

Weapons

  • Click a weapon or press 1–9.
  • What each one does is listed at the bottom of this page, and under its name while you aim.
  • The cannon never runs out; everything else is limited.
  • A direct hit deals 50% extra damage — and the enemy gets the same bonus on you.
  • The green badge on a weapon is its upgrade level.

Cannon mods

  • At cannon level 3 the shell can roll after it lands; at level 5 it can ricochet instead.
  • Toggle with R and B, or the pills above the weapon bar.
  • Only one can be active at a time.
  • A rolling shell that crests a ramp launches into the air.

Flares

  • F pops flares. Two per match.
  • P pauses, M shows your achievements mid–match.
  • They only break a Seeker's lock — nothing else is fooled.
  • The button pulses when a seeker is in the air.

Supply crates

  • Yellow refills your emptiest weapon.
  • Red hands over a special: nuke, flame pillar, seeker or kamikaze.
  • Drive over one to take it — or shell it to deny the enemy.
  • Red drops arrive every 2–4 rounds.

Fire and fallout

  • Burning ground and radioactive fallout only hurt the tank whose turn it is.
  • So you can sit out a fire during the enemy's turn — then drive clear on yours.
  • Fire hurts more than fallout. A flame pillar's column burns anyone standing in it.

Wind and weather

  • The gauge shows wind strength and direction; it changes every turn.
  • Turn on weather disasters for gales, sandstorms, lightning and meteors.
  • In a gale a headwind can stall a shell mid–air and blow it back at you.
  • Storms pay 40% more scrap.

Game modes

  • Duel — one on one against the CPU, or two players hot–seat.
  • Waves — survive as long as you can. Every 5 waves adds another hostile, and they arrive with upgraded weapons.
  • You keep your tank between waves with a patch–up and fresh flares.
  • Hidden enemy weapon masks what the CPU is about to fire, and pays 25% more.

Scrap and the garage

  • You earn scrap from hull remaining, the difficulty you chose, and any bonuses.
  • Spend it on new chassis, weapon levels, and the three stat tracks.
  • Weapon upgrades are stored per chassis.
  • Levels 3 and 5 add a special perk; the ABILITY track sharpens each tank's signature trait.
